https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.who: Becca (then Brent) Royal-Gordon, later an SE-0168 co-author
https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.where: swift-evolution mailing list, thread "multi-line string literals.", message 015738
https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.says: Recalls that Perl 6's redesign took a heredoc's base indentation from the indentation of its delimiter, and asks whether Swift should treat multi-line literals the same way.

https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.who: John Holdsworth, later SE-0168's lead author
https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.where: swift-evolution mailing list, thread "multi-line string literals.", message 016646
https://lists.swift.org/pipermail/swift-.says: Proposes that the lexer strip each line's margin by the whitespace that precedes the closing quote, explicitly as Perl 6 does.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.who: John Holdsworth, Becca Royal-Gordon and Tyler Cloutier, authors; Joe Groff, review manager
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0168, Multi-Line String Literals
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Specifies triple-quoted multi-line strings whose lines all lose the indentation found ahead of the closing delimiter; the text never mentions Perl or Perl 6.

https://forums.swift.org/t/accepted-se-0.who: Joe Groff, review manager, for the Swift core team
https://forums.swift.org/t/accepted-se-0.says: Accepts the proposal with revisions: where the closing delimiter sits fixes the indentation for the whole literal, and under-indented or inconsistently indented lines are errors. Perl goes unmentioned.

http://www.rubyist.net/~matz/20050722.ht.where: Matz's diary on rubyist.net, entry on the new lambda grammar (Japanese)
http://www.rubyist.net/~matz/20050722.ht.says: Traces the original arrow-lambda proposal to Perl 6, explains Perl 6's pointy-block closures and loops, calls Perl 6 culturally close to Ruby, yet doubts when or whether it will be used.

https://github.com/ruby/ruby/commit/759a.says: Adds an arrow lambda expression to Ruby's parser and records it in the ChangeLog as a Perl6-style lambda, flagged as new and very experimental.

https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-dev/266.where: ruby-dev mailing list, message 26650 (Japanese), thread on Ruby 2.0 block-parameter notation
https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-dev/266.says: Replying to Shin-ichiro Hara, who wanted parameters listed within the braces, Matz says the present grammar follows Perl 6, sets the Perl6/Ruby2 arrow form beside Groovy's and Haskell's, and offers to reconsider.

https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.where: ruby-core mailing list, message 16734, thread "lambda, ->, haskell, and so on"
https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.says: Answering Evan Phoenix, Matz confirms Perl 6 has the arrow syntax and is its source, and says he once tried an arrow block form for method calls but dropped it as too radical.

https://wiki.php.net/rfc/saner-inc-dec-o.who: George Peter Banyard, the RFC's author
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/saner-inc-dec-o.where: PHP RFC: Path to Saner Increment/Decrement operators
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/saner-inc-dec-o.says: Sets PHP's string increment beside Raku's, describing Raku as a Perl successor whose result is consistent, and states that the proposed PHP behaviour follows Raku's.

https://gist.github.com/milseman/bb39ef7.who: Michael Ilseman, Apple engineer leading Swift's String and standard-library work
https://gist.github.com/milseman/bb39ef7.where: GitHub gist "State of String: ABI, Performance, Ergonomics, and You!"
https://gist.github.com/milseman/bb39ef7.says: Sets Swift the aim of surpassing Perl at string processing, cites Apocalypse 5, and lists Perl 6 regex features Swift should take outright, from free-form syntax and named captures to interpolation, plus ratcheting and LTM.

https://forums.swift.org/t/declarative-s.who: Michael Ilseman, lead designer of Swift's string processing
https://forums.swift.org/t/declarative-s.where: Swift Forums, "Declarative String Processing Overview", post #46
https://forums.swift.org/t/declarative-s.says: Says the earlier literal design drew heavily on Raku, but familiar, conventional regex syntax mattered most for literals, so the team's novelty budget goes to Pattern, though he prefers Raku's syntax himself.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.who: Hamish Knight and Michael Ilseman, authors
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0355, Regex Syntax and Run-time Construction
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Defines the regex syntax Swift accepts in literals and strings as a blend of PCRE 2, Oniguruma, ICU and .NET, compares behaviour with Perl in places, and never mentions Raku or Perl 6.

https://metacpan.org/pod/release/STEVAN/.says: States that Moose grew out of the experimental prototypes Little built for Perl 6's meta-model, while stressing that Moose itself is meant for real use rather than as an experiment.

https://web.archive.org/web/202402081301.where: Joose.Manual, Joose 3.013 documentation on openjsan.org (Wayback copy of 8 Feb 2024; the live URL now serves an unrelated page)
https://web.archive.org/web/202402081301.says: Presents Joose as a complete JavaScript object system modelled largely on Moose, which it credits with borrowing much from Perl 6's object model as well as from CLOS and Smalltalk.

https://forums.swift.org/t/optional-dict.who: Becca (then Brent) Royal-Gordon, later an SE-0168 co-author
https://forums.swift.org/t/optional-dict.where: swift-evolution thread on multi-line string literals, imported to Swift Forums under the title "Optional dictionary subscripts", post #21
https://forums.swift.org/t/optional-dict.says: Arguing against copying Perl 5's quoting rules into Swift, Royal-Gordon recounts helping design Perl 6, serving as pumpking for a subsystem of Parrot, and contributing patches to Perl 5 itself.

https://forums.swift.org/t/review-se-016.where: Swift Forums, SE-0168 review thread, post #17
https://forums.swift.org/t/review-se-016.says: Surveying prior art during the review, Royal-Gordon describes Perl 6's quoting as Perl 5's arbitrary delimiters and heredocs with de-indentation and user-defined quoting added, noting that Perl 5 lacks de-indenting.

http://www.rubyist.net/~matz/20050701.ht.says: Listing candidate lambda notations, Matz sketches a Perl6-style anonymous function with the arrow before its parameters and judges Perl 6's arrow an acceptable shorter alternative to a lambda keyword, alongside Haskell's backslash.

https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.who: Evan Phoenix, Rubinius lead developer, quoting Matz
https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.where: ruby-core mailing list, message 16733, thread "lambda, ->, haskell, and so on"
https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.says: Evan Phoenix quotes Matz saying he is content with the current arrow and that sharing it with Perl 6 would quickly win mind-share, then asks whether Perl 6 actually has that syntax.

https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.where: ruby-core mailing list, message 16766, thread "lambda, ->, haskell, and so on"
https://blade.ruby-lang.org/ruby-core/16.says: Rejecting David A. Black's objection that the mind-share argument would equally justify Perl's globals, Matz replies that Perl 6 has good ideas worth taking even though its bad parts are very bad.

https://externals.io/message/68160#68184.who: Peter Lind, PHP internals list participant
https://externals.io/message/68160#68184.where: PHP internals list, thread "Allow letter decrementing", message 68184
https://externals.io/message/68160#68184.says: Citing Perl 6's Synopsis 3 in a thread on letter decrementing, Lind notes that Perl 6 can decrement strings, though not as a full mirror image of its increment.

https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.who: Chris Lattner, Swift's creator, core team
https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.where: Swift Forums (swift-evolution import), "Empower String type with regular expression", post #4
https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.says: Lattner hopes Swift gains proper regex support and argues that first-class language support would allow inline captures, flexible syntax, compile-time checking and Perl 6-style extensions beyond the basic regex model.

https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.who: Chris Lattner, Swift's creator, core team
https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.where: Swift Forums (swift-evolution import), "Empower String type with regular expression", post #9
https://forums.swift.org/t/empower-strin.says: Lattner urges readers to study Perl 6's regexes, explaining that a community obsessed with regexes got to rebuild them from experience and produced something very powerful.

https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.who: Chris Lattner, Swift's creator, core team
https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.where: Swift Forums (swift-evolution import), "Strings in Swift 4", post #130
https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.says: Agreeing with Joe Groff, Lattner says Swift has much to gain from Perl 6's grammars and should take its time on them, adding that by regex he means a general grammar system.

https://forums.swift.org/t/regular-expre.who: Chris Lattner, Swift's creator, core team
https://forums.swift.org/t/regular-expre.where: Swift Forums, "Regular expressions in Swift", post #10
https://forums.swift.org/t/regular-expre.says: Lattner says Perl 6 has excellent ideas for regex support after long community thought, and that although the language is not widely used, Swift should study and learn from its strengths.

https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.where: Swift Forums (swift-evolution import), "Strings in Swift 4", post #68
https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.says: Groff warns against a narrow focus on regexes, says the Perl 6 designers grew regex support into arbitrary grammars, and recommends Swift begin from that level by examining their work.

https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.where: Swift Forums (swift-evolution import), "Strings in Swift 4", post #153
https://forums.swift.org/t/strings-in-sw.says: Abrahams explains that regexes cannot parse languages like Swift and that he has in mind parsers of the kind Perl 6's recursive grammars allow, linking examples.

https://forums.swift.org/t/pitch-regex-s.who: Joe Groff, Swift team, replying to Hamish Knight's pitch
https://forums.swift.org/t/pitch-regex-s.where: Swift Forums, Regex Syntax pitch thread, post #2 (the pitch itself is Hamish Knight's)
https://forums.swift.org/t/pitch-regex-s.says: Groff backs a PCRE baseline, singles out free-whitespace /x mode as the most valuable tweak, and notes that Raku made it the default for pattern literals, urging new languages to do likewise.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.who: Hamish Knight, Michael Ilseman and David Ewing, authors
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0354, Regex Literals
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Enables extended (?x) syntax, with non-semantic whitespace and comments, in multi-line #/…/# literals, and rejects that default for single-line ones for familiarity and compatibility; it cites Perl, never Raku.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.who: Richard Wei, Michael Ilseman, Nate Cook and Alejandro Alonso, authors
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0351, Regex builder DSL
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Introduces RegexBuilder, a result-builder DSL for assembling regexes from reusable components, including other regexes and custom patterns, without mentioning Perl or Raku.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0350, Regex Type and Overview
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Calls Parsing Expression Grammars the nearest formal analogue of Swift's regex design, which uses ordered-choice alternation, possessive quantification and recursive subpattern calls; it never mentions Perl or Raku.

https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.who: Nate Cook and Alejandro Alonso, authors
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.where: Swift Evolution proposal SE-0363, Unicode for String Processing
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolu.says: Compares Swift's grapheme-cluster regex matching with NSString, Java, Ruby and Perl, and lists a reference link to Raku's regex documentation that nothing in the proposal's text uses.

https://github.com/python/cpython/issues.who: Matthew Barnett, author of the third-party regex module
https://github.com/python/cpython/issues.says: Barnett reports that his re-engine rework adds backward matching so lookbehinds can be variable-width, and credits the idea to a page on implementing it in Perl 6, without naming the page.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.who: Synopsis 5 (Larry Wall, Damian Conway, Patrick Michaud and others), Perl 6 design document
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.when: Created 24 Jun 2002; passage present in the 6 Apr 2006 mirror
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: States that the after assertion performs lookbehind by matching a reversed syntax tree leftward, and forbids lookbehind on any pattern that is not reversible.

https://pypi.org/project/regex/.who: Matthew Barnett, the regex module's author
https://pypi.org/project/regex/.says: Describes regex, a separately installed package, as an alternative intended to replace Python's built-in re, compatible with it but adding features, among them lookbehinds able to match strings of varying length.

https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/propos.who: eddyb (Eduard-Mihai Burtescu), Rust language and compiler team member
https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/propos.where: Rust internals forum, "Proposal: Grammar Working Group", post #8
https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/propos.says: Describing the proposed grammar notation, eddyb lists separator forms for repeated items and says the % syntax comes from Perl 6, as he recalls, having been suggested by eternaleye.

https://github.com/rust-lang/wg-grammar/.who: Rust Grammar Working Group (eddyb, Eric Huss, Mazdak Farrokhzad)
https://github.com/rust-lang/wg-grammar/.says: The working group's expression grammar writes comma-separated lists, among them array elements, tuple fields, call and method arguments and closure parameters, with the %% separator modifier.
